dek.text: Of {{number:c27:2}} data centers in the Tribune's count, {{number:c29}} never returned the water board's mailed survey. ERCOT's new request carries the board's questions to data centers not yet energized.

introduction.text: [Records the Texas Tribune obtained for 2020 through 2025 identified {{number:c27:2}} unique data center facilities](c27). [By the Tribune's count {{number:c28}} of them submitted the water board's use survey at least once](c28). [The other {{number:c29}} never submitted a requested survey](c29).

[ERCOT dated its Market Notice M-B091426-01 on {{date:c1}}](c1). [It carries water questions that ERCOT says it wrote with the utility commission and the water board](c12), [and ERCOT says it will pass the answers to the board](c15). [The request goes to data centers that are proposed or not yet energized](c4), [while the survey reaches only data centers that were operating in the year surveyed](c40).

sections.heading: A mailed survey with a small fine

paragraphs.text: [The Tribune reported that the survey goes to operating facilities using more than {{number:c38}} million gallons a year](c38). [The water board says state law requires everyone who receives it to submit a completed one](c47). [Its FAQ names data centers among the industrial users that must](c50).

[Skipping the survey can bring a Class C misdemeanor charge, the Tribune reported](c30), [with a fine of up to {{money:c31}}](c31). [The board says it has no authority of its own to prosecute](c32). [Local officials are left to decide whether to bring a case](c34). [State officials don't know whether any misdemeanor penalty has been issued against a data center](c35).
[Last year {{number:c45}} facilities completed the survey and reported {{number:c45:1}} billion gallons of water between them](c45).

sections.heading: A request that comes through the grid

paragraphs.text: [The notice is addressed to developers of data centers of {{number:c3}} MW and larger](c3). [It reaches developers of proposed data centers with a peak requested load of at least {{number:c4}} MW and under {{number:c4:1}} MW](c4). [A transmission or distribution provider has to have classified that load as Substantiated Load](c5). [It also reaches data centers ERCOT conditionally classified in its Batch Zero interconnection process](c6) [if they have not yet energized at {{number:c7}} kV or above](c7).

[Each transmission or distribution provider files the response for the developer](c21). [A complete response had to include a notarized attestation](c20). [Responses were due by {{number:c19}} p.m. on {{date:c19}}](c19). [Any failure to respond will be reported to the utility commission and the Office of the Governor](c23). [The notice cites the Texas Water Code for any failure to fully answer the water questions](c17) [and warns that such a failure may expose a recipient to criminal penalties](c18).

sections.heading: What the record can't show yet

paragraphs.text: [The survey reaches operating facilities](c40) [and the request reaches proposed ones and those not yet energized](c4). Neither the notice nor the Tribune's reporting says the {{number:c29}} facilities that never returned a survey will be asked by ERCOT. [ERCOT says it will work with the utility commission on a report of conclusions from its review](c25). [It expects to publish that report by {{date:c26}}](c26). The report does not exist yet.

[Raising the misdemeanor fine would take state legislation, the Tribune reported](c36). [Lawmakers don't meet in Austin until January](c37). [Governor Abbott has said he will work to put his executive actions into law when the Legislature returns](c56). That is a stated intention, not a law.
